Getting Started with Color Themes

Source: vignettes/articles/colortheme.Rmd
colortheme.Rmd

Color themes

The "colortheme" object provides two color-generating functions: palette() and ramp(). The palette() function accepts an integer nn and returns a vector of nn discrete colors. It is primarily intended for qualitative themes, where distinct colors are used to represent categorical data. The ramp() function accepts a numeric vector xx with values in the [0,1][0, 1] interval and returns a vector of corresponding colors. It maps numeric values onto a continuous color gradient (or stepped color bands), making it suitable for sequential and diverging themes as well as binned scales.

Pre-defined themes

You can get a pre-defined "colortheme" object by providing a theme name to the colortheme() function.

library(colortheme)
# diverging color theme "azurerose" (package:colortheme)
azurerose <- colortheme("azurerose")
print(azurerose)
#> Diverging Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #005AAD, #3B78C2, #729BD6, #AFC4E8, #F7F7F7, #E8B3CC, #D67FA8, #BD4989, #A4136E
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 9L
#>   palette.formatter: "interpolate"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "ramp"
#>   alpha: NA

The palette and ramp functions are accessible via $ operator.

azurerose$palette(5)
#> [1] "#0059AC" "#729AD6" "#F7F7F7" "#D67FA7" "#A4136D"
azurerose$ramp(seq.int(0, 1, by = 0.1))
#>  [1] "#0059AC" "#3371BD" "#5E8CCE" "#8BABDD" "#BDCDEB" "#F7F7F7" "#EBC0D4"
#>  [8] "#DD93B6" "#CC6A9B" "#B84083" "#A4136D"
# sequential color theme "viridis" (package:viridisLite)
viridis <- colortheme("viridis")
print(viridis)
#> Sequential Color Theme: 'viridis' (from 'viridisLite')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: palette
#> 
#> Kernel Function:
#> function (n, alpha = 1, begin = 0, end = 1, direction = 1, option = "D")
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : Inf
#>   reverse.method   : "kernel.args$direction <- - kernel.args$direction"
#>   palette.formatter: "interpolate"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   option   : "viridis"
#>   alpha    : 1
#>   begin    : 0.2
#>   end      : 0.8
#>   direction: 1

The palette and ramp can also be extracted using corresponding helper functions; as_palette() and as_ramp().

as_palette(viridis)(5)
#> [1] "#414487FF" "#2F6C8EFF" "#21908CFF" "#2FB47CFF" "#7AD151FF"
as_ramp(viridis)(seq.int(0, 1, by = 0.1))
#>  [1] "#404486" "#39548C" "#32658D" "#2C728D" "#26818D" "#21908C" "#1F9F87"
#>  [8] "#26AC80" "#39B976" "#57C665" "#79D151"

You can modify themes by reversing the color order or changing the theme type (e.g., from sequential to qualitative). Note that converting a theme to @qualitative also turns its $ramp() into a stepped (binned) color ramp by default. These changes can be applied in two ways:

  1. Using Arguments : provide the appropriate argument to the function, such as reverse = TRUE or type = "qualitative".
  2. Using Suffixes : for convenience, you can append a suffix directly to the theme’s name. _r to reverse the theme, @q (or longer, such as @qual) to make the theme qualitative (@d for diverging, @s for sequential).
#> Qualitative Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #A4136E, #BD4989, #D67FA8, #E8B3CC, #F7F7F7, #AFC4E8, #729BD6, #3B78C2, #005AAD
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 9L
#>   palette.formatter: "recycle"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "palette"
#>   alpha: NA

#> Qualitative Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #A4136E, #BD4989, #D67FA8, #E8B3CC, #F7F7F7, #AFC4E8, #729BD6, #3B78C2, #005AAD
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 9L
#>   palette.formatter: "recycle"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "palette"
#>   alpha: NA

You can also customize kernel arguments and option parameters on the fly using query parameters after ? (e.g., "highlight?which=1:2" or "viridis?ramp.steps=5").

colortheme("viridis", type = "q", kernel.size = 7, begin = 0, end = 1)
#> Qualitative Color Theme: 'viridis' (from 'viridisLite')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: palette
#> 
#> Kernel Function:
#> function (n, alpha = 1, begin = 0, end = 1, direction = 1, option = "D")
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 7
#>   reverse.method   : "kernel.args$direction <- - kernel.args$direction"
#>   palette.formatter: "recycle"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   option   : "viridis"
#>   alpha    : 1
#>   begin    : 0
#>   end      : 1
#>   direction: 1

colortheme("viridis@qual?kernel.size=7;begin=0;end=1")
#> Qualitative Color Theme: 'viridis' (from 'viridisLite')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: palette
#> 
#> Kernel Function:
#> function (n, alpha = 1, begin = 0, end = 1, direction = 1, option = "D")
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 7
#>   reverse.method   : "kernel.args$direction <- - kernel.args$direction"
#>   palette.formatter: "recycle"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   option   : "viridis"
#>   alpha    : 1
#>   begin    : 0
#>   end      : 1
#>   direction: 1

By setting ramp.steps (either as an integer for equal bins or as a numeric vector of cutoffs in (0,1)(0, 1)), any continuous theme can be quantized into a stepped color ramp:

# Quantize into 5 equal steps
colortheme("azurerose?ramp.steps=5")
#> Diverging Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #005AAD, #3B78C2, #729BD6, #AFC4E8, #F7F7F7, #E8B3CC, #D67FA8, #BD4989, #A4136E
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 9L
#>   palette.formatter: "interpolate"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : 5
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "ramp"
#>   alpha: NA


# Split at custom cutoffs to create a desired ramp
colortheme("azurerose?ramp.steps=seq.int(.4, .6, by=.02)")
#> Diverging Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #005AAD, #3B78C2, #729BD6, #AFC4E8, #F7F7F7, #E8B3CC, #D67FA8, #BD4989, #A4136E
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 9L
#>   palette.formatter: "interpolate"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : c(0.4, 0.42, 0.44, 0.46, 0.48, 0.5, 0.52, 0.54, 0.56, 0.58, 0.6)
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "ramp"
#>   alpha: NA

When multiple packages provide a theme with the same name (e.g., "Paired"), you can specify which one to use in two ways:

  1. Using Argument : provide the package name to the source argument (e.g., source = "grDevices").
  2. Using Prefix : prepend the package name and a forward slash to the theme name (e.g., "RColorBrewer/Paired").
# qualitative color theme "Paired" (package:grDevices)
colortheme("Paired", source = "grDevices")
#> Qualitative Color Theme: 'Paired' (from 'grDevices')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: palette
#> 
#> Kernel Function:
#> function (n = NULL, palette = "Okabe-Ito", alpha, recycle = FALSE, names = FALSE)
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 12L
#>   palette.formatter: "recycle"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : 12
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   palette: "Paired"
#>   alpha  : NULL
#>   recycle: FALSE

# qualitative color theme "Paired" (package:RColorBrewer)
colortheme("RColorBrewer/Paired")
#> Qualitative Color Theme: 'Paired' (from 'RColorBrewer')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #A6CEE3, #1F78B4, #B2DF8A, #33A02C, #FB9A99, #E31A1C, #FDBF6F, #FF7F00, #CAB2D6, #6A3D9A, #FFFF99, #B15928
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 12L
#>   palette.formatter: "recycle"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : 12
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "palette"
#>   alpha: NA

Custom themes

Alternatively, you can create a new "colortheme" object by passing a custom color vector or function to the first argument of colortheme().

# create a new color theme using a color vector
mytheme <- colortheme(
  c("#003f5c", "#7a5195", "#ef5675", "#ffa600"),
  type = "sequential", name = "mytheme"
)
print(mytheme)
#> Sequential Color Theme: 'mytheme'
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #003f5c, #7a5195, #ef5675, #ffa600
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 4L
#>   palette.formatter: "interpolate"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "ramp"
#>   alpha: NA

as_palette(mytheme)(5)
#> [1] "#003F5B" "#614D86" "#B85485" "#F46C63" "#FFA500"
as_ramp(mytheme)(seq.int(0, 1, by = 0.1))
#>  [1] "#003F5B" "#33456C" "#534B7D" "#704F8F" "#94528E" "#B85485" "#D9557B"
#>  [8] "#F15F6E" "#F77857" "#FB8F3B" "#FFA500"
# create a new color theme using a color function
rainbow <- colortheme(
  grDevices::rainbow,
  name = "rainbow", source = "grDevices"
)
print(rainbow)
#> Sequential Color Theme: 'rainbow' (from 'grDevices')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: palette
#> 
#> Kernel Function:
#> function (n, s = 1, v = 1, start = 0, end = max(1, n - 1)/n, alpha, rev = FALSE)
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : Inf
#>   palette.formatter: "interpolate"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA

as_palette(rainbow)(5)
#> [1] "#FF0000" "#CCFF00" "#00FF66" "#0066FF" "#CC00FF"
as_ramp(rainbow)(seq.int(0, 1, by = 0.1))
#>  [1] "#FF0000" "#FF9800" "#CCFF00" "#35FF00" "#00FF64" "#00FFFB" "#006AFF"
#>  [8] "#2F00FF" "#C600FF" "#FF009D" "#FF0006"

You can register a custom theme to call it by name later in your current R session. To do so, use the register_colortheme() function.

register_colortheme(mytheme, name = "mytheme", source = "custom")
colortheme("custom/mytheme@q")
#> Qualitative Color Theme: 'mytheme' (from 'custom')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #003f5c, #7a5195, #ef5675, #ffa600
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 4L
#>   palette.formatter: "recycle"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "palette"
#>   alpha: NA

colortheme("mytheme_r@div?alpha=.5")
#> Diverging Color Theme: 'mytheme' (from 'custom')
#> 
#> Kernel Class: color
#> 
#> Kernel Colors:
#> #ffa600, #ef5675, #7a5195, #003f5c
#> 
#> Options:
#>   kernel.size      : 4L
#>   palette.formatter: "interpolate"
#>   palette.reverse  : FALSE
#>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1)
#>   ramp.steps       : Inf
#>   na.color         : NA
#>   reverse.method   : NA
#> 
#> Kernel Arguments:
#>   mode : "ramp"
#>   alpha: 0.5

Using themes with ggplot2

To apply your color themes to ggplot2 plots, use the scale_color_theme() and scale_fill_theme() functions. These scales integrate your themes directly into the plot’s color and fill aesthetics.

library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal())

set.seed(42)
dataset <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 5000L), ]

p <- ggplot(dataset) + geom_point(aes(carat, price, col = color))
p + scale_color_theme("shiki")

p + scale_color_theme("viridisLite/mako", discrete = TRUE)

p + scale_color_theme("tokyo@qual")

p + scale_color_theme("highlight?which=list(1, 6:7);base='00000000'")

p2 <- ggplot(dataset) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = carat, fill = cut), bins = 20)
p2 + scale_fill_theme("ukiyoe")

p2 + scale_fill_theme("highlight_r?which=list(1:2, 5)")

p2 + scale_fill_theme("ai@q")

p2 + scale_fill_theme("Zissou 1_r@q")

# Continuous and stepped scales with sequential, diverging, and qualitative themes
p3 <- ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() + theme(legend.position = "right")
p3 + scale_fill_theme("ai")

p3 + scale_fill_theme("Cividis", middle = 0.02)

p3 + scale_fill_theme("steps", middle = 0.02)

p3 + scale_fill_theme("magma?ramp.steps=6&alpha=0.8")
